meaning: Something that is very easy to do.
sentence: The English test was a piece of cake.

meaning: To face a difficult situation with courage.
sentence: I hate going to the dentist, but I just have to bite the bullet.

meaning: Good luck, especially in a performance.
sentence: Before I went on stage, my friend whispered, 'Break a leg!'

meaning: To stop working on something.
sentence: It's getting late, let's call it a day.

meaning: To do something perfunctorily to save time or money.
sentence: Don't cut corners when building a house; safety is paramount.

meaning: Slow down; be careful.
sentence: Easy does it with that glass vase; it's very fragile.

meaning: Get out of control.
sentence: The party got out of hand when uninvited guests arrived.

meaning: Work better or leave.
sentence: You need to get your act together if you want to pass this exam.

meaning: Trust someone's word without proof.
sentence: I didn't have proof, so I decided to give her the benefit of the doubt.

idiom: Hit the nail on the head
meaning: Describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem.
sentence: You hit the nail on the head with your analysis of the market.

meaning: You're better off not knowing some things.
sentence: Sometimes ignorance is bliss when you don't want to worry about gossip.

idiom: Kill two birds with one stone
meaning: To accomplish two different things at the same time.
sentence: By walking to the grocery store, I killed two birds with one stone: exercise and shopping.

idiom: Let the cat out of the bag
meaning: To share a secret unintentionally.
sentence: We wanted to surprise her, but John let the cat out of the bag.

meaning: Happens very rarely.
sentence: He eats fast food once in a blue moon because he prefers healthy cooking.

meaning: Something good that isn't recognized at first.
sentence: Missing that flight turned out to be a blessing in disguise.

meaning: People's intentions can be judged better by what they do than what they say.
sentence: He promises to help, but actions speak louder than words.

meaning: To make a bad situation worse.
sentence: Not only did I miss my bus, but to add insult to injury, it started pouring rain.

meaning: It is up to you to make the next decision or step.
sentence: I've made my offer; now the ball is in your court.

meaning: Looking in the wrong place or accusing the wrong person.
sentence: If you think I took your keys, you're barking up the wrong tree.

meaning: Avoiding the main topic; not speaking directly.
sentence: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what you really think.

meaning: All the advantages of two different things at once.
sentence: Working from home gives her the best of both worlds: career flexibility and family time.

idiom: Bite off more than you can chew
meaning: Take on a commitment you cannot fulfill.
sentence: Taking three advanced classes and working part-time means he bit off more than he could chew.

meaning: Damaging a relationship beyond repair.
sentence: Never burn bridges when leaving a company, as you never know who you'll work with again.

idiom: By the skin of your teeth
meaning: Barely escaping a disaster.
sentence: He passed the driving test by the skin of his teeth.

meaning: A problematic situation from which there is no escape by problem-solving because of mutually conflicting conditions.
sentence: You need experience to get a job, but you need a job to get experience—it's a classic catch-22.

meaning: A change in one's attitude or opinion.
sentence: He had a change of heart and decided to donate to the charity.

meaning: Pursue your ambitions passionately.
sentence: Don't let fear stop you from chasing your dreams.

meaning: Holding a grudge or grievance.
sentence: He walks around with a chip on his shoulder, always ready to argue.

meaning: No matter what happens.
sentence: I will be there to support you, come rain or shine.

meaning: Complaining about a past loss or failure that cannot be undone.
sentence: We lost the match, but there's no use crying over spilled milk.

meaning: Being too inquisitive can lead to danger or trouble.
sentence: Don't ask too many personal questions; remember, curiosity killed the cat.

meaning: Get to the point without wasting time.
sentence: Let's cut to the chase and discuss the budget.

meaning: A candidate or competitor of whom little is known but who unexpectedly wins.
sentence: Few expected her to win the championship, but she proved to be a dark horse.

meaning: Someone who takes a contrary position just for the sake of argument.
sentence: I agree with your plan, but let me play devil's advocate for a moment.

meaning: A very small, inadequate amount compared to what is needed.
sentence: Donations were helpful, but they were just a drop in the bucket.

meaning: Not as easy to do as it is to talk about.
sentence: Losing weight sounds simple, but it's easier said than done.

meaning: An obvious problem that no one wants to discuss.
sentence: Everyone ignored the budget deficit, treating it like the elephant in the room.

idiom: Every cloud has a silver lining
meaning: Every bad situation has some good aspect to it.
sentence: I lost my phone, but finding a twenty-dollar bill on the street proved every cloud has a silver lining.

meaning: Accept the unpleasant consequences of one's actions.
sentence: He knew he cheated on the exam and had to face the music.

meaning: Be abandoned or neglected.
sentence: His hobby fell by the wayside once he started working two jobs.

meaning: Very different from.
sentence: This quiet cabin is a far cry from the noisy city.

idiom: Feel a bit under the weather
meaning: Feel slightly ill.
sentence: I won't be coming to work today because I'm feeling a bit under the weather.

meaning: Become nervous or hesitant before a big event.
sentence: Right before the wedding, he got cold feet.

meaning: Intentionally ignore someone.
sentence: She was upset with him and gave him the cold shoulder all evening.

meaning: Make an extra effort to achieve something.
sentence: Our customer service team always goes the extra mile to help clients.

meaning: A natural talent for growing plants.
sentence: Her garden is always blooming because she has a real green thumb.

meaning: Have a wonderful time.
sentence: We had an absolute blast at the amusement park.

meaning: Daydreaming or unaware of reality.
sentence: He never pays attention in class; his head is always in the clouds.

meaning: Go to bed.
sentence: I'm exhausted; I think it's time to hit the sack.

meaning: Wait a moment; be patient.
sentence: Hold your horses! Let me explain before you jump to conclusions.
